questions.stem: Which item is NOT a programming paradigm?
questions.solution: Debugging is an activity, not a programming paradigm.

questions.stem: How many times does a while loop execute when its condition is false initially?
questions.solution: while is a pretest loop; a false condition skips the body.

questions.stem: Which identifier is valid in C++?
questions.solution: An identifier may contain letters, digits and underscores, but cannot start with a digit or be a keyword.

questions.stem: Which statement immediately exits a loop?
questions.solution: break terminates the nearest loop or switch.

questions.stem: Which declaration creates a floating-point variable named price?
questions.solution: float is used for real numbers.

questions.stem: Which operator reads data from cin?
questions.solution: The extraction operator >> reads from an input stream.
% is the modulus operator and returns the remainder.

questions.stem: Which part of a for loop is executed after each iteration?
questions.solution: The update expression runs after each iteration.

Machine code produced by an assembler
questions.solution: Pseudocode expresses algorithm logic without strict language syntax.

questions.stem: Which loop is commonly used to process every array element?
questions.solution: A for loop with an index visits each element.

questions.stem: This question tests the program development life cycle.

parts.text: Define source code and object code.
parts.answer: Source code is the human-readable program text; object code is the machine-oriented output produced by a compiler.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Describe THREE stages of the program development life cycle.
parts.answer: Analysis (requirements), design (algorithm/flowchart), coding (implementation), testing (verification), maintenance (updates). Any three stages.
parts.solution: Award 1 mark for each correctly described stage.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A program reads a student's score from 0 to 100 and displays the grade: 80-100 A, 60-79 B, 50-59 C, 40-49 D, below 40 F.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the grade classification.
parts.answer: Start -> read score -> decision score >= 80 -> A; else score >= 60 -> B; else score >= 50 -> C; else score >= 40 -> D; else F -> display grade -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for terminal symbols, input, four/five decisions, each output and correct flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode for the algorithm and convert it into a complete C++ program.
parts.answer: IF score >= 80 THEN grade = A ELSE IF score >= 60 THEN grade = B ... ENDIF; use if/else if in C++ and display grade.
parts.solution: Award marks for correct pseudocode, complete C++ structure, conditions, input and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests type conversion and constants.

parts.text: Explain the difference between implicit and explicit type conversion, and give one C++ example of each.
parts.answer: Implicit conversion is automatic (int to double); explicit conversion uses a cast such as double(total) or static_cast<double>(total).
parts.solution: Award marks for both definitions and valid examples.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a C++ program segment that calculates the average of three integer marks as a double and displays it to two decimal places.
parts.answer: double average = (m1 + m2 + m3) / 3.0; cout << fixed << setprecision(2) << average;
parts.solution: Award marks for floating-point division, fixed/setprecision and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Trace the program and show the exact output.
parts.solution: Award marks for each line and the exact row lengths.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Identify TWO logic errors in a version that prints four rows but reuses j without resetting it. Rewrite the corrected code.
parts.answer: The inner loop must initialise j = 1 for every row and the outer loop must run to 4. Correct code: for (int i=1;i<=4;i++){for(int j=1;j<=i;j++) cout<<j; cout<<endl;}
parts.solution: Award marks for each error and the corrected loop.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A shop stores the prices of five items in an array.

parts.text: Declare an array named prices with the values 20.5, 55.0, 15.9, 75.0 and 10.0. Display all values.
parts.answer: double prices[5] = {20.5, 55.0, 15.9, 75.0, 10.0}; for (int i=0;i<5;i++) cout << prices[i] << endl;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct type, initialiser, loop and output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment that applies a 10% discount to prices above RM50 and stores the results in a second array. Display both arrays.
parts.answer: double sale[5]; for(int i=0;i<5;i++){ sale[i] = prices[i] > 50 ? prices[i]*0.9 : prices[i]; } then display both arrays.
parts.solution: Award marks for second array, condition, discount, preservation and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A bookstore records up to five books. Each book has a title, price and quantity in stock.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.

parts.text: Define a struct Book. Write a complete C++ program that reads the records, calculates the total inventory value, and displays the title of the most expensive book.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.

questions.stem: A lecturer records the marks of ten students in an array.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 4 for total/average, 3 for highest/index, 3 for above-average count and 2 for output.

parts.text: Write a complete C++ program that reads ten marks, displays the average, the highest mark and its index, and counts how many marks are above the average.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 4 for total/average, 3 for highest/index, 3 for above-average count and 2 for output.
